team.summary: Four co-founders with YC W20 experience; CEO Harry Qi has venture/angel background, COO Ethan Yu brings quantitative trading expertise, CTO Chander Ramesh implies technical leadership, but no founder has a prior exit or deep vertical experience in AI agents for SMBs.

founders.name: Harry Qi
founders.background: Co-founder and CEO of Motion; YC W20; previously associated with Pioneer Fund as LP/Venture Partner and active angel investor.

founders.name: Ethan Yu
founders.background: Co-founder and COO of Motion; previously a quantitative trader at DRW and Citadel; YC W20.

founders.name: Omid Rooholfada
founders.background: Co-founder of Motion; no further background details found in sources.

founders.name: Chander Ramesh
founders.background: Co-founder and CTO of Motion; technical depth implied by CTO role, but prior startups/exits not found.

team.technicalDepth: CTO in place suggests in-house engineering capability, but no public evidence of owning core model/integration layer; likely relies on third-party LLM APIs.

product.plainLanguage: Motion is an AI work platform that has added AI agents aimed at SMBs, presumably to automate tasks end-to-end rather than just assist.
product.category: AI productivity / AI agent platform for SMBs

market.sizeHint: SMB productivity software market is large (hundreds of billions globally), but no specific TAM figure provided.
market.competitiveLandscape: Crowded: Notion AI, ClickUp, Asana, Monday.com, and numerous vertical AI agent startups targeting SMB workflows.
market.whyNow: LLM cost/performance improvements enable affordable agentic workflows; SMBs increasingly open to AI automation.

risks.text: Highly competitive market with well-funded incumbents adding AI agents
Dependence on third-party LLM providers for core intelligence
Unproven product differentiation and switching costs for SMBs
Limited evidence of proprietary data or workflow lock-in

subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: Founders have YC experience and strong individual backgrounds (quant, venture), but lack prior exits and direct domain expertise in AI agents for SMBs. Technical depth is implied but not demonstrated.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: One-liner is clear; AI agents suggest action-oriented product; self-serve SMB onboarding plausible but unconfirmed.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: Large SMB productivity market; why-now driven by LLM advances; wedge is AI agents for SMBs, but competitive landscape is intense.

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: $38M Series C led by Scale Venture Partners is a strong recent signal; however, no public data on paying customers, active usage, or community engagement.

scoreRationale: Motion shows promising funding traction and a credible team pedigree, but scores low on defensibility and only modestly on product differentiation and market wedge. The overall profile suggests a venture-backed startup in a crowded space with unproven moats.
